v2ToTaxonomyMappingUsedForComparison.necessity: V2's native code output uses matchStatus/representationStatus enum values (UNREPRESENTED, PARTIAL, EXACT_SINGLE, EXACT_COMPOSITE, HONESTLY_UNRESOLVED, AMBIGUOUS, CONTRADICTORY), not the second-pass protocol's 9-state vocabulary directly - V2's own production matching code was correctly never modified to emit a different vocabulary (that would be a production/evaluator-matching-logic change, forbidden after seeing results, and was never attempted). A translation was therefore required to perform the detailed comparison at all.

UNREPRESENTED_subSplit.rule: V2's own already-computed reasonForNoCredit text (frozen in 06-frozen-sample-labels-live-SEALED.json's v2Reason field, written in the SAME run that produced the frozen packets, BEFORE the second-pass reviewer was dispatched) already distinguishes three patterns in its own wording, corresponding exactly to the three states 02-state-taxonomy.json already defined before this rerun: '...explicitly flag the gap...' -> REVIEW_REQUIRED_FLAG_ONLY; '...every one of them is inventory-only...' -> DISCOVERY_ONLY_NOT_REPRESENTED; '...Nothing represents this claim...' -> UNSUPPORTED_SILENT.
UNREPRESENTED_subSplit.integrityNote: This pattern-match rule was derived and finalized BEFORE the agreement numbers were computed, from data (V2's own reasonForNoCredit strings) that was itself frozen before the second-pass reviewer's judgments were seen. It is a mechanical extraction of a distinction V2's matching.ts logic had already made internally, not a discretionary choice made to influence the outcome - it was applied uniformly to all 18 UNREPRESENTED cases in the sealed labels with zero manual overrides or exceptions.

v2ToTaxonomyMappingUsedForComparison.goldenPathVerification: Attempted a full mechanical replay from the frozen packets' own embedded semanticJudgeOutputs (docs/evaluation-v2-iteration/06-frozen-sample-full-unit-detail-INTERNAL.json) to cross-check this text-pattern rule against a from-scratch recomputation; the replay could only recover 52 of the original 592 judge outputs (buildEvidencePacket's evidence packets, by design, retain judge outputs only for the trimmed top-5-candidate view, not all originally-evaluated pairs) and was therefore insufficient for a full independent cross-check. The text-pattern rule above is the one actually used; this limitation is disclosed rather than hidden.

whyDetailedAgreementGotNumericallyWorseD: 01-original-disagreement-forensics.json's headline finding was that 65.6% of the ORIGINAL detailed disagreements were pure vocabulary mismatches (V2 had a richer disposition set than the second-pass reviewer's old 6-option rubric). This phase gave the reviewer V2's own richer vocabulary specifically to remove that artifact. It worked in the sense that the reviewer now correctly distinguishes 'HONESTLY_UNRESOLVED'-style states from plain non-existence - but doing so surfaced a NEW, finer-grained, genuine disagreement: V2's own internal criteria for what counts as REVIEW_REQUIRED_FLAG_ONLY vs DISCOVERY_ONLY_NOT_REPRESENTED vs UNSUPPORTED_SILENT (or CONTRADICTORY) do not match a careful independent reviewer's criteria for the same three-way (or four-way) distinction, even though almost all of these disagreements (31 of 39, 79.5%) leave the CREDIT decision unchanged. This is real progress on the specific problem the taxonomy fix targeted (see the false-credit gate result below) revealing a DIFFERENT, previously-invisible-because-masked-by-vocabulary-mismatch calibration gap underneath it.

knownFalseCreditRegressionOnThisRun.note: All 14 confirmed Phase 3F.1.1 false credits present in this 51-case sample remain correctly rejected on BOTH sides - V2's live-informed labels AND the second-pass reviewer's independent judgments.
knownFalseCreditRegressionOnThisRun.notableImprovement: doc-a::VI::6.10-chapeau (the case that Phase 3F.1.5's original second-pass reviewer incorrectly re-credited, reproducing a confirmed historical false credit) was this time correctly classified DISCOVERY_ONLY_NOT_REPRESENTED (no credit) by the new, independently-dispatched reviewer. This is direct evidence that the new protocol's abstract worked example on the discovery-vs-representation distinction (05-second-pass-protocol.json) is doing real, effective work, even though the overall agreement gate still misses its thresholds for other reasons.
